Predicted seagrass carbon map at Cadiz Bay for 2024 and 2025

Lee, Chengfa Benjamin

2026-05-13

This page documents the results of the Zostera noltii seagrass carbon mapping work at Cadiz Bay. This includes work done in:

  • Coring Carbon Seagrass by Simon Oiry
  • Exploring the relationship between seagrass reflectance and biomass
  • Measuring the carbon content in Zostera noltii seagrass

All analyses were performed in R version 4.5.2 (R Core Team 2025). All work belong to the REWRITE project.

1 Study Location

This page focuses on Cadiz Bay, a demonstrator site for the REWRITE PROJECT. There is an extensive seagrass meadow along the bay.

The sites were sampled according to transect lines.

2 Seasonal change

Figure 2.1: Mean NDVI value of pixels classified by the ICE CREAMS model as seagrass in 2024 and 2025. The black line denotes the actual mean NDVI values while the blue line and grey ribbons are the geom_smooth values. The dotted red line indicates the chosen date (2025-06-14) for showcasing the analyses.

Figure 2.2: Total seagrass extent of pixels classified by the ICE CREAMS model as seagrass in 2024 and 2025, by assuming that every percent in the seagrass cover is equivalent to 1 m^2. The black line denotes the predicted extent while the blue line and grey ribbons are the geom_smooth values. The dotted red line indicates the chosen date (2025-06-14) for showcasing the analyses.

3 ICE CREAMS Model prediction

For the purpose of map display and data analysis, the result from the Sentinel-2 image on 14 June 2025 was chosen. This date falls within the fieldwork dates and is thus best for validation and groundtruthing.

5 Carbon stock prediction

Table 5.1: Seagrass biomass and carbon at Cadiz Bay. “DW” denotes the dry weight of the seagrass samples while “C” denotes the carbon in the seagrass samples. The total carbon estimate included the aboveground carbon estimate, belowground carbon estimate and the soil carbon estimate. The soil carbon estimate was extracted from the soil carbon values in Cadiz Bay reported in Santos et al. (2023), which was based on the upper 1m sediment layer.

Figure 6.1: Predicted biomass values of the aboveground, belowground and total components of the seagrass meadows in Cadiz Bay from 2016 to 2025.

Figure 6.2: Predicted carbon values of the aboveground and belowground components of the seagrass meadows in Cadiz Bay from 2016 to 2025.
